source.paper: FinEvo-Bench: A Longitudinal Benchmark for Self-Evolving Agents in Professional Financial Workflows

paper_evidence.benchmark_scope: 120 real-case-grounded tasks, 20 business scenes across six financial domains; six related but substantively distinct cases per scene.
paper_evidence.controls: Four self-evolving scaffolds use the same Qwen3.7-Max backbone over three independently shuffled globally interleaved streams, with paired non-evolving controls intended to estimate retained-experience gain.
paper_evidence.evaluation: Paper states outputs are scored by an independent Claude Code scoring agent backed by Claude Opus 4.6 using manually reviewed task-quality and financial-compliance rubrics.
paper_evidence.reported_results: Across scaffolds, evolving conditions improve scores by +9.33 to +19.37 and reduce compliance issues by 0.12-0.44/task; ranks 4-6 exceed ranks 1-3 paired gains by 6.10-8.70; Claude Code skill-only beats memory-only and combined memory+skill; rubric feedback beats reference-answer feedback across all four scaffolds.
paper_evidence.top_cells: Letta evolved score 91.65 with 0.09 compliance issues/task; Codex largest self-evolution gain +19.37 according to the paper.

reproducibility_assessment.official_artifact_support: no public implementation or benchmark repository identified in the targeted search
reproducibility_assessment.judgment: FinEvo-Bench provides methodologically valuable longitudinal controls in the paper, but reproducibility is currently much weaker than for the code-released candidates audited in the same pipeline. The arXiv record does not link source code, targeted searches did not locate an official benchmark repository, and public paper-index services currently expose a 'Request Code' state. Because tasks are partly grounded in institution-provided professional procedures/cases and evaluation uses hosted agent/judge systems, the exact benchmark corpus, stream permutations, scaffold configurations and scoring stack cannot be reconstructed from public executable artifacts located in this pass. The quantitative gains should therefore remain primary-study evidence with a strong reproducibility caveat.
exact_blockers: No official code or benchmark data repository was linked from the arXiv abstract or located in targeted public searches as of 2026-08-25.

The task corpus depends on institution-provided professional procedures and eligible institution-provided/public cases; exact task bytes, provenance, rubrics and access conditions were not located as a public versioned artifact.
Exact three-stream shuffled task orderings and paired evolving/non-evolving run manifests were not located publicly.
The four scaffold implementations/configurations used with Qwen3.7-Max were not located as a released experiment harness in this pass.
Scoring depends on Claude Code backed by hosted Claude Opus 4.6, adding provider/judge drift and requiring exact judge prompts/configuration for replay.
No independent public reproduction of the +9.33 to +19.37 score gains, compliance reductions, late-vs-early rank effects, skill-vs-memory ablation or feedback-type ablation was found.
Third-party awesome-list entries and paper digests are discovery/summary evidence, not reproductions.
reproducibility_assessment.scope: Do not downgrade the paper's internal matched-control design merely because code is absent; reproducibility strength and experimental-design strength are separate. But do not promote any FinEvo quantitative cell to replicated evidence until versioned task/rubric/run artifacts or an independent rerun become available. Finance-specific procedural reuse may not generalize to unrelated domains.

downstream_note: For Integrator/evidence scoring, preserve FinEvo as a strong longitudinal-design candidate but apply a reproducibility penalty relative to executable candidates. The skill-only > memory-only/combined and rubric-feedback > reference-answer findings are especially decision-relevant hypotheses, yet currently remain paper-only quantitative claims.
